analysis.investment_thesis: Anup Engineering is a technically credible specialty fabricator serving high-growth end-markets (LNG, hydrogen, pharma), with a 62-year track record and 24.5% revenue CAGR — but at 34.8x P/E with deeply negative FY25 free cash flow and inherently lumpy project-based economics, you're paying a compounder price for a cyclical business. A fair business at an unfair price is no bargain.
key_strengths: Revenue CAGR 24.5% over 5Y with operating margins expanding from ~28% to 23% EBITDA — genuine operating leverage
Diversified end-markets (oil & gas, LNG, hydrogen, aerospace) and proprietary tech products (Helix Changer, EMBaffle) suggest some pricing power above commodity fabricators
Conservative balance sheet historically — D/E 0.25, zero debt through FY2022, reserves compounding at a healthy clip
key_risks: Catastrophic FCF quality in FY2025: OCF = -₹7 Cr vs Net Profit ₹118 Cr — FCF/NI ratio deeply negative, exposing the working capital trap inherent in project-based businesses
Borrowings surged from ₹0 to ₹158 Cr in FY2025 during capacity expansion — execution risk and return-on-new-capital unproven
Valuation at 34.8x P/E and 22.4x EV/EBITDA leaves zero margin of safety for a cyclical industrial where order books can evaporate quickly
red_flags: FY25 Operating CF turned negative (-₹7 Cr) despite ₹118 Cr net profit — earnings are not converting to cash, a Munger cardinal sin
FCF has been negative in 2 of the last 3 years (FY23: -₹45 Cr, FY25: -₹51 Cr) — this is not a predictable cash compounder
Gross margin reported at 3.79% is anomalously low — either data reflects a pass-through materials cost structure or accounting requires deeper scrutiny
analysis.detailed_analysis:
Invert first: what kills this investment? A project-based fabricator with lumpy order flows, working capital intensity, and zero pricing power over raw materials (evidenced by the 3.79% gross margin) can look profitable on an accrual basis while burning cash for years. FY2025 is exhibit A — ₹118 Cr net profit, negative operating cash flow, ₹51 Cr negative FCF, and borrowings that ballooned from zero to ₹158 Cr. This isn't a compounding machine; it's a capital-hungry cyclical dressed in growth clothing. ROCE of 18.26% and ROE of 18.9% are decent but not exceptional, and they'll be tested as the new capacity must earn returns on a significantly enlarged asset base.

On the positive side, there is genuine business quality here. Anup has carved a niche in technically demanding custom process equipment, serves marquee industries with high switching costs on individual projects, and has grown revenue nearly 3x in five years. The proprietary technology products (Helix Changer, EMBaffle licensed from HTRI) add a layer of differentiation above plain-vanilla fabricators. However, the market has fully priced this in at 6.36x book and 34.8x earnings — multiples that demand consistent, high-quality cash earnings. Until FCF normalizes post-expansion and demonstrates that the new capacity earns above 15% ROIC, the risk/reward for new capital is mediocre at best.
